en_title: The Witcher 3 Devs Talk Songs of the Past DLC Details
opus_summary: 《巫师3》第三个资料片《旧时曲》计划于2027年推出，带来全新地区、怪物和故事。CDPR开发者谈及新地区的文化与环境设计，并表示团队会与世界观设定团队合作，在保持设定一致的同时探索新故事。

paragraphs.en: It's been more than a decade since The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt was first released, but CD Projekt Red isn't quite finished with the game just yet. Songs of the Past , the game's third expansion, is set to arrive in 2027, bringing with it an entirely new region to explore, new monsters to hunt, and more stories to tell.
paragraphs.cn: 距离《巫师3：狂猎》首次发售已经过去了十多年，但CDPR还没有完全结束对这款游戏的开发。游戏的第三部资料片《旧时曲》计划于2027年推出，带来一片可供探索的全新区域、新的狩猎怪物，以及更多有待讲述的故事。

paragraphs.en: But how do you expand on a game as beloved as The Witcher 3 without upsetting its notoriously dedicated fans? And how do you keep things fresh while remaining faithful to a universe with decades of established lore?
paragraphs.cn: 但要如何为《巫师3》这样一款深受喜爱的游戏扩展内容，又不惹恼那些出了名忠实的粉丝？又要如何在忠于一个拥有数十年既定设定的世界观的同时，保持新鲜感？

paragraphs.en: IGN spoke to CD Projekt Red's level design lead Miles Tost and Songs of the Past writer Paula Meissner at the Lucca Comics & Games festival about creating a distinct new corner of the Continent, the surprising importance of local booze, and why even bringing characters back from the dead doesn't necessarily mean breaking canon.
paragraphs.cn: 在Lucca Comics & Games展会上，IGN采访了CDPR关卡设计负责人Miles Tost和《旧时曲》编剧Paula Meissner，谈及如何在大陆上打造一个独具特色的新角落、当地酒水出人意料的重要性，以及为什么即便让角色死而复生，也不一定意味着违背既定设定。

paragraphs.en: IGN: Talking about Songs of the Past, from a pure level design perspective, is there a special new mechanical hook that you're looking at for players? And also, how does the environment actively change in a way that maybe veteran players of The Witcher 3 are going to be finding something new?
paragraphs.cn: IGN：说到《旧时曲》，从纯粹的关卡设计角度来看，你们是否正在考虑为玩家设计某种特别的新机制亮点？另外，环境会如何发生实际变化，让《巫师3》的老玩家或许也能发现新东西？

paragraphs.en: Miles Tost: Generally speaking, the introduction of a whole new region. And if you've played the base game and the other expansions, for us, these regions are really fun. I think they have a lot of answers for that question by themselves because we try to always make each one feel unique, not just visually, but in the sense of the traversal. Skellig, for example, has a lot of boat travel as a reliance. It's also very mountainous. No Man’s Land is a much wider space. And I think with the value of Lettin, you'll basically see also that as you move around — we're not introducing a new motion mechanic as far as I'm aware — but generally it's really important to us that when you are in an area, you have this distinct feeling of being in this space.
paragraphs.cn: Miles Tost：总体来说，就是引入一个全新的区域。如果你玩过本体游戏和其他资料片，对我们来说，这些区域真的很有意思。我认为它们本身就为这个问题提供了很多答案，因为我们一直努力让每个区域都有独特的感觉，不仅在视觉上如此，在穿行的体验上也是如此。例如，Skellig很大程度上依赖乘船出行，那里也多山。No Man’s Land则是一片开阔得多的空间。我认为，Lettin的价值也会让你在四处移动时基本感受到这一点——据我所知，我们不会引入新的移动机制——但总体而言，对我们来说非常重要的是，当你身处一个区域时，能有一种身在这片空间的鲜明感觉。

paragraphs.en: And this goes further culturally, for example. The people of Lettin have their own cultural backdrop. There are some British influences in the aristocracy there, but also we have very, very many Polish countryside influences there. You see that in the architecture, and we usually go pretty deep in thinking about the cultural identity of these spaces. So with Skellig, we have the more Viking-esque influences, but here, these people have their own alcohol.
paragraphs.cn: 比如，这一点在文化层面上还会进一步体现。Lettin的居民有自己的文化背景。那里的贵族阶层受到了一些英国文化的影响，但我们也加入了非常、非常多的波兰乡村元素。你可以从建筑中看到这一点，而我们通常会相当深入地思考这些空间的文化身份。因此，在Skellig，我们采用了更多维京风格的元素，而在这里，这些人有他们自己的酒。

paragraphs.en: It's a fun thing to mention because — Bracket is what it's called — it's a kind of fusion between honey and beer. It feels like such a small thing, but for us it's very important, because it draws a lot on what this region is. So for the production of it, you need honey and you need hops. And so you will find both of these in the area. And other than it being a cultural export, of the area and the economical backbone of the place, it even changes how we think about monsters there. So in the demo we've shown, we're basically introducing one new monster, the Swarmion, and these guys love honey. They use hornets as a means of protection, all that stuff. And so the logical reason there is because what kind of monster would live there? So the Swarmion makes sense. So you find that this seemingly small thing of these guys having their own alcohol, and it really has this huge effect on the entire area. And so this is a bit of how we're trying to make things feel unique and special. And it goes into the quest storytelling and all of that.
paragraphs.cn: 这是一件提起来很有意思的事，因为——这种酒叫Bracket——它是蜂蜜和啤酒的一种融合。这看起来是件很小的事，但对我们来说非常重要，因为它在很大程度上取材于这个地区本身的特点。要酿造这种酒，你需要蜂蜜和啤酒花。所以你能在该地区找到这两样东西。除了作为该地区的文化输出和当地的经济支柱，它甚至改变了我们对那里的怪物的构思方式。在我们展示的演示中，我们基本上介绍了一种新怪物Swarmion，这些家伙喜欢蜂蜜。它们用大黄蜂来保护自己，诸如此类。而其中的逻辑是：什么样的怪物会住在那里？所以Swarmion是合理的。于是你会发现，这些人有自己的酒，这件看似微小的事情，实际上对整个地区产生了巨大影响。这也在一定程度上体现了我们如何努力让事物显得独特而特别。这也会延伸到任务叙事等各个方面。

paragraphs.en: IGN: Obviously, The Witcher has maybe one of the deepest lores in fiction, with lots of established canon. With Songs of the Past, was there a particular piece of deep lore that was particularly tricky to untangle? And as you were putting all this together, did you have to bend any of the established canon to make the story fit?
paragraphs.cn: IGN：显然，《巫师》或许拥有虚构作品中最深厚的设定之一，其中有大量既定的正史内容。在制作《旧时曲》时，有没有哪一段深层设定特别难以梳理？在把这一切整合起来的过程中，你们是否不得不对既定正史做出一些变通，让故事能够契合？

paragraphs.en: Paula Meissner: We actually do have an amazing lore team in CDPR that we are cooperating with. And these guys are just amazing. They know everything, every detail from the books, from every game, from every piece of franchise content. So we do talk with them on a regular basis to make sure that we don't say anything stupid and that we stay actually truthful to the lore. But yeah, it is a tricky question because it touches on topics that weren't revealed yet. So there were definitely challenges, but I don't know how much I can say about those.
paragraphs.cn: Paula Meissner：事实上，CDPR确实有一支很棒的设定团队，我们一直在和他们合作。这些人真的很厉害。他们无所不知，了解书籍、每一款游戏以及这个系列每一项内容中的每一个细节。所以我们会定期和他们交流，确保我们不会说出什么蠢话，也确保我们确实忠于设定。不过，是的，这个问题很难回答，因为它涉及尚未公开的话题。所以肯定是有挑战的，但我不知道自己能谈多少。

paragraphs.en: Miles Tost: The general thought is that we try to always also evolve and make things fresh. So it's really important for us to not really think in this way of like, “Oh, can we do this or can we not? If we do, how? How would we bring Regis back?" If we just told people before Blood and Wine, "Yeah, we're going to do it." A lot of the hardcore fans would probably go like, "That's impossible. He fucking vaporized. How would he?" And I think we asked ourselves those same questions, and ultimately I think we settled on something that works as an expectation where he's like, "Yeah, he's back, but he's like 10% of his power, and he's still recovering. He's only been able to recover because he's had help from this other higher vampire."
paragraphs.cn: Miles Tost：总体思路是，我们也一直努力发展变化，让事物保持新鲜感。所以对我们来说，非常重要的一点是，不要真的以这样的方式思考：「哦，我们能不能这么做？如果要做，该怎么做？我们要怎样让Regis回来？」如果我们只是在《血与酒》推出前告诉大家：「对，我们要这么做。」很多铁杆粉丝可能会说：「这不可能。他他妈都化成灰了。他怎么回来？」我想我们也问过自己同样的问题，而最终我认为我们确定了一个符合预期的可行方案，大致是：「对，他回来了，但他的力量只剩下大约10%，而且他还在恢复。他之所以能够恢复，是因为得到了另一名高等吸血鬼的帮助。」

paragraphs.en: Geralt, by himself, is already like, "Hey, let's just bring him back from the dead." And it works as long as you can explain it and make it make sense. And I think this is really the approach that we're trying to take. So we don't really try to retcon things, but we do try to find cool ways to expand and build on the franchise and the established lore as long as we can find ways to explain it.
paragraphs.cn: Geralt本身就已经像是在说：「嘿，我们干脆让他死而复生吧。」只要你能够解释清楚，让事情合情合理，这样做就是可行的。我认为这正是我们努力采取的方法。所以我们并不是想要追溯性地修改设定，而是想在能够找到解释方法的前提下，寻找很酷的方式来扩展和发展这个系列及其既定设定。

paragraphs.en: Paula Meissner: We often actually use discussing challenges with the lore team as [original Witcher author] Andrzej Sapkowski would do it. If you look at the books and lore of The Witcher in the books, it's such a mix of everything, to be honest. And even if you hear Sapkowski in interviews and people ask him these questions, he's often like “Whatever.” So yeah, this is the ultimate argument that we use sometimes, and sometimes it works.
paragraphs.cn: Paula Meissner：实际上，我们经常在和设定团队讨论难题时，采用《巫师》原著作者Andrzej Sapkowski会采取的做法。如果你看看《巫师》的书籍和书中的设定，老实说，那真是什么都有的大杂烩。而且如果你听过Sapkowski接受采访，当人们问他这些问题时，他经常会说「随便」。所以，是的，这是我们有时会使用的终极论据，有时候还挺管用。
